subject.title: Gateway auto-injects toolsAllow into isolated agentTurn crons; null patch doesn't clear it; breaks CLI backend

question: How should OpenClaw repair CLI-backed cron jobs that carry flagless `toolsAllow` from the regression window without making explicit per-cron restrictions fail open?
rationale: The remaining availability problem is source-reproducible, but distinguishing stale auto-default caps from intentional explicit restrictions changes a security boundary and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Add narrow stale-default repair
options.body: Add a doctor/operator or tightly scoped migration path that only marks or clears provably auto-default regression-window cron caps while preserving explicit restrictions as fail-closed.

options.title: Broaden null-clear authority
options.body: Allow the agent-facing `toolsAllow: null` path to bypass creator-surface re-capping, accepting a broader authority change that needs explicit security approval.

options.title: Document manual recreate or clear
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and document that affected jobs must be recreated or cleared through a trusted operator path.

recommendation.title: Add narrow stale-default repair
recommendation.body: Add a doctor/operator or tightly scoped migration path that only marks or clears provably auto-default regression-window cron caps while preserving explicit restrictions as fail-closed.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the most recent marker-preservation edit semantics and are closest to the current safety split.
